principle: ONE ATLAS, MULTIPLE LEGAL ONTOLOGIES. Each collection declares its own native structural model here. atlas-core.js reads this registry to navigate every collection without hardcoding hierarchy levels. NOTE: the meta.<field> VALUE already contains the correct Thai structural word (e.g. 'บรรพ 3', 'ภาค 2', 'หมวด 1'); the 'label' in each level below is for UI chrome (pickers, filter headers, breadcrumb chips, aria) and for legal-correctness of level naming — it is NOT used to rewrite the stored value.

aviation.storageKeyModel: Multi-instrument collections key codex-data.json articles as "<instrumentId>::<number>" (e.g. books.aviation.articles["act::12"], ["mr::12"]). Single-instrument collections are unchanged (key == number). Legacy viewer id for a multi provision is "<collection>_<instrumentId>::<number>" (e.g. aviation_act::12) — still one "_" split, so codex-article-viewer.html keeps working unchanged.
aviation.notes: ARCHITECTURE DEMONSTRATION ONLY — enabled:false. No articles exist in codex-data.json books.aviation yet. This entry proves that a future multi-instrument collection (Act + Emergency Decree + Ministerial Regulation + Announcement + CAAT Requirement + Standard), each with its own provision unit (มาตรา vs ข้อ) and its own internal levels, is expressible purely through registry configuration. atlas-core.js excludes planned/disabled collections from listCollections() and every corpus operation until real data is added.
